previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with dysuria, fever, chills, and right flank pain following recent completion of Bactrim for a prior UTI. She has a complex medical history including recurrent UTIs with chronic cystitis, HIV, hepatitis B and C, morbid obesity, and chronic pain. Urinalysis showed pyuria and bacteriuria, and preliminary urine culture grew >100,000 colonies of E. coli. Given her history of resistant infections, she was treated with IV imipenem after initial ceftriaxone in the ED. Symptoms resolved during the two-day admission, and she completed eight doses of antibiotics. Chronic issues including HIV, anticoagulation with warfarin, and pain management were maintained on home regimens. She was discharged home with instructions to continue all medications, take phenazopyridine for three days, monitor weight, and follow up with her primary care provider for final culture results and INR monitoring.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old female with a complex PMH (see 
below), who has been feeling sick for 2 days now- chest 
tightness, shortness of breath, nonproductive cough and dysuria. 

  
#1. Ili with asthma exacerbation: DFA for influenza was 
negative. Her exam and history were consistent with an asthma 
exacerbation in the setting of an Ili. She was treated with 
nebs, and methylprednisolone initially and transitioned to 
prednisone, and azithromycin. Her respiratory status improved 
overnight. She remained afebrile, and was off of supplemental 
oxygen. She was discharged on a regimen of azithromycin x 5 
days, prednisone taper 40 for 1 day, 30 for one day, 20 for one 
day, 10 for one day, and as needed nebulizer treatments.

#2. Syphilis: Her PCP discovered an RPR of 1:1 with confirmatory 
positive, and she was started on doxycyline for 30 days. She 
continued on doxycycline while admitted and was scheduled to 
continue until ___. 

#3. Dysuria: chronic colonization and dysuria, admitted 
frequently with UTIs. She has had varying culture data, most 
recently with Bactrim sensitive bugs. She was given Bactrim in 
the ED and a foley was placed. Urine culture grew E. Coli. It 
was thought to be her chronic colonization. Bactrim was 
discontinued prior to discharge. Her foley was discontinued and 
she passed plentiful urine prior to discharge.  

#4. HIV: Last CD4 count >900, last viral load undetectable. On 
HAART. She was  continued on her outpatient regimen Atazanavir 
300 mg daily, Emtricitabine-Tenofovir (Truvada) 1 tab daily, 
RiTONAvir 100 mg PO daily.
 
#5. Constipation: Aggressive regimen at home given chronic 
narcotics. Continued home regimen. 

#6. Pain: On methadone and dilaudid at home. Continued. 

#7. Anxiety/Depression: On escitalopram and clonazepam at home. 
Continued home medications. 

#8. OSA: History of CPAP, but no recent use. Will offer use and 
order CPAP for hospitalization.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Shortness of breath and fever.  Evaluate for pneumonia.

TECHNIQUE:  Upright AP and lateral radiographs of the chest.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior radiographs of the chest, most recent ___.

FINDINGS:

The exam is severely limited by the patient's body habitus. The right
costophrenic sulcus on anterior view and posterior costophrenic sulci on later
view are not imaged.  Within the limits of this study, the lungs appear well
expanded.  A linear opacity in the left mid lung is unchanged, likely
scarring/chronic atelectasis.  Interstitial markings are exaggerated due to
overlying soft tissue, however there are no definite focal opacities to
suggest pneumonia.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette and hilar contours are
unchanged.  The heart size is exaggerated on the AP view.  There is no large
pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:

Study limited by body habitus and an incompletely imaged costophrenic sulci,
however there is no evidence of acute cardiopulmonary process.
